Watts made this hymn from Psalm 90:13–17, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

13Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants. 14Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days. 15Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil. 16May Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children. 17May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish for us the work of our hands— yes, establish the work of our hands! PSALM 90:13–17 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 90
Return, O God of love, return; Earth is a tiresome place: How long shall we thy children mourn Our absence from thy face! STANZA I
